claims.head: A tough night ahead for Kaprizov
claims.call: The Flames’ P1 (Bahl and Nemec) spends at least 43% of its 5-on-5 time against the Wild’s first line.
claims.body: At home, the Flames keep sending Bahl and Nemec out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Huska has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Wild’s first line is Ek, Kaprizov and Boldy.

claims.gist: At home, Ryan Huska likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Wild’s first line.

notes.text: Marcus Foligno is on injured reserve and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Jared Spurgeon is out (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Jonas Brodin has taken his spot beside Quinn Hughes.
Brock Faber is on injured reserve (skull surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-pair defenseman. Jonas Brodin has taken his spot beside Quinn Hughes.
Tyler Pitlick was added to the roster on Oct 13 and has played beside Michael McCarron and Yakov Trenin.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 7 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 45%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Samuel Honzek is out week to week (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Yegor Sharangovich has taken his spot beside Mikael Backlund and Joel Farabee.
Joel Hanley has not dressed for the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Jake Middleton has taken his spot beside Zayne Parekh.
Jonathan Huberdeau is on injured reserve (hip surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, up from 2% last season.

CGY.head: Not an easy night for the Flames
CGY.body: Even though Calgary has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Flames can pull it off if they keep the shots coming.

MIN.head: The Wild have a lot going for them
MIN.body: Even though Calgary has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Flames’ way back in is piling up shots.

items.text: Blake Coleman faces Calgary for the first time since leaving.
Jake Middleton faces Minnesota for the first time since leaving.

The Wild are newly without Jared Spurgeon, have been without Marcus Foligno since Oct 8, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson and Brock Faber all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start.
The Flames are newly without Samuel Honzek, have been without Joel Hanley since Oct 3, and have had to make do without Jonathan Huberdeau all season.
